dev.architecture_decision_rationale: User directive 2026-05-09: harness work for project-specific gaode-maps ban should not pollute global dot-claude shared with multi-asset-portfolio and other projects. Split into two layers: (1) project-local policy + matcher library + hook for the 8 gaode_* keys + 6 surfaces — fully self-contained, reads only from $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/policies/gaode-policy.json; (2) global residual: roles.timeline + roles.transportation in tool-policy.v1.json kept because the global hook still needs to recognize these travel-planner-specific agents for the standard role-table check (allowed_tools / denied_tools). Without the global role entries the global tool-policy hook would deny Write to legitimate timeline.json paths (timeline agent role would be 'unknown role') OR allow Write/Edit to bypass the Feb-13-2026 incident lock (no denied_tools entry).
dev.verifier_chaining_decision: T2/T3 production reality: BOTH the global pretool-tool-policy.py AND the project-local pretool-gaode-policy.py fire on every tool call (different settings.json layers). Verifier chains them in order [project-local, global]. Project-local-first because gaode-policy is conceptually a strictly additive precondition layer; global handles standard role-table afterwards. Ordering matters for cases like AC11.6 (Gmail body env-var scan) where the global hook would otherwise block at tool-not-in-allowed_tools BEFORE the gaode env-var matcher gets a chance to fire.
